<details>
<summary>Compare a sample in one minute</summary>
	1. **Hook:** what musical gesture do you remember?
	2. **Texture:** where does the weight or atmosphere come from?
	3. **Reaction:** what draws you in, and what reduces your interest?
	Report the edition and whether you sampled tracks or heard the full album. Leave a score blank unless you choose to give one.
</details>
<details>
<summary>Six sound cues</summary>
	### Rhythm and grip
	Follow the pulse, then the bass line. Catchiness might come from a recurring bass figure, a drum accent, or the vocal phrasing. Name the element holding your attention.
	### Attack and weight
	Attack is the initial strike of a note or drum hit. Weight concerns the impression of depth and force. Loud playback, strong bass, distorted guitars, and hard drumming do not always produce the same effect.
	### Guitar texture
	Distinguish sharp rhythmic strokes, ringing melodic lines, abrasive noise, and sustained layers. A heavily effected guitar does not automatically mean a heavier song.
	### Space and atmosphere
	Reverb gives a sense of space and decay. Delay adds repeated echoes. Listen for the balance between close, immediate sounds and distant layers.
	### Voice and character
	Notice register, urgency, theatrical phrasing, and restraint. Sinister atmosphere might come from delivery rather than lyrics or low pitch alone.
	### Hooks and identity
	Identify the moment you remember after the track ends. Then ask what separates the band from others you enjoy: rhythm, tone, melody, arrangement, or vocal character.
</details>

## 🌐 Sources for the wider scene {color="purple"}
Checked <mention-date start="2026-10-09"/>. Use artist/label pages for dates, credits, editions, and artwork; use editorial sources for interviews and attributed listening opinions.
<columns>
	<column ratio="50">
		### News, interviews & record discoveries
		- [Post-Punk.com](https://post-punk.com/) — Gothic rock, post-punk, darkwave, and related scenes. Follow a news story back to the artist’s release page.
		- [Bandcamp Daily](https://daily.bandcamp.com/) — Features, label profiles, scene reports, and editorial selections. Start with [Six Gloomy Gems From the Dark Punk Revival](https://daily.bandcamp.com/lists/dark-punk-revival-list), an older scene guide connecting punk and deathrock.
		- [CVLT Nation](https://cvltnation.com/cvlt/about/) — A broad underground magazine. Useful for darker punk and crossover discovery; check each record’s genre and format.
	</column>
	<column ratio="50">
		### Reviews, history & adjacent sounds
		- [I Die: You Die](https://www.idieyoudie.com/) — Reviews, track roundups, and the We Have a Technical podcast. Useful for darkwave, ethereal, and electronic comparisons.
		- [Deathrock.com](https://deathrock.com/) — Profiles of 45 Grave, Christian Death, Ausgang, and other historical leads. Its homepage says the site is rebuilding; use it as a research starting point.
		- [Side-Line: Shadows Veil’s Fallen](https://www.side-line.com/shadows-veil-fallen-album/) — An example of current release coverage, with a tracklist and Bandcamp player. The broader site covers adjacent electronic music too.
	</column>
</columns>
**Research habit:** save the article’s author/date and direct URL, then verify the original release date and edition on the artist/label page. A review is someone’s opinion; tags are discovery clues, and your journal holds your own reaction.

	### Rhythm and grip
	Follow the pulse, then the bass line. Catchiness might come from a recurring bass figure, a drum accent, or the vocal phrasing. Name the element holding your attention.
	### Attack and weight
	Attack is the initial strike of a note or drum hit. Weight concerns the impression of depth and force. Loud playback, strong bass, distorted guitars, and hard drumming do not always produce the same effect.
	### Guitar texture
	Distinguish sharp rhythmic strokes, ringing melodic lines, abrasive noise, and sustained layers. A heavily effected guitar does not automatically mean a heavier song.
	### Space and atmosphere
	Reverb gives a sense of space and decay. Delay adds repeated echoes. Listen for the balance between close, immediate sounds and distant layers.
	### Voice and character
	Notice register, urgency, theatrical phrasing, and restraint. Sinister atmosphere might come from delivery rather than lyrics or low pitch alone.
	### Hooks and identity
	Identify the moment you remember after the track ends. Then ask what separates the band from others you enjoy: rhythm, tone, melody, arrangement, or vocal character.
